title: At-least-once means duplicates
goal: The outbox guarantees delivery at least once — never exactly once. So every consumer has to be idempotent. That is a contract, not an optimisation.
startWith: Step 10 finished: the outbox publishes reliably.

newIdeas.plain: Every message arrives, and some arrive more than once. It is what you get from any system that retries, which is every real system. Exactly-once across two systems is not available, however it is marketed.
Processing the same message twice has the same effect as processing it once. Sending one email, not two. Charging one card, not two.

A table keyed on (event_id, consumer_group). Inserting is the check: the primary key makes a second insert fail, and that failure is your signal to skip. Keyed by group because each consumer group must process the message independently.

newIdeas.term: The dedupe write and the business write must share a transaction
newIdeas.plain: If they are separate, you can mark a message processed and then fail the work — or do the work and fail to mark it. You have moved the dual-write bug down one layer instead of fixing it.
When a consumer joins or leaves, partitions are reassigned. Anything in flight may be reprocessed by the new owner. This is the ordinary, everyday reason duplicates happen — no failure required.

tasks.do: Reproduce duplicates by replaying the topic
tasks.why: Rewinding a consumer group takes one command and shows you exactly what a rebalance would do.
tasks.how: Notification-service needs somewhere to record what it did, so give it a table first — remove the DataSource exclusion you added in step 07. Count the rows, rewind the group to the start, count again. The count doubles. Nothing failed; the system worked exactly as designed.

blocks.label: notification: give it a database
blocks.body:
mkdir -p services/notification-service/src/main/resources/db/migration
cat > services/notification-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__sent.sql << 'EOF'
CREATE TABLE sent_notifications (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    hold_id     UUID        NOT NULL,
    sent_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
EOF
# and remove the DataSourceAutoConfiguration exclusion from application.yml,
# adding:  spring.datasource.url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/notification

blocks.label: Count, rewind, count again
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-postgres psql -U ledgerflow -d notification \
  -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sent_notifications;"

kill $(lsof -ti:8082)                       # a group can only be rewound while idle
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk group seek notification-service --to start
./mvnw -pl services/notification-service spring-boot:run

sleep 15
docker exec -it lf-postgres psql -U ledgerflow -d notification \
  -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sent_notifications;"

check.expect: The count doubled. Every customer just got a second email.

tasks.why: The consumer needs a memory, and the database's primary key is the cheapest reliable one there is.
tasks.how: Composite primary key on (event_id, consumer_group). You are not writing dedupe logic — you are letting the database enforce uniqueness and treating the constraint violation as the answer.

blocks.label: services/notification-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__processed_events.sql
blocks.body:
cat > services/notification-service/src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__processed_events.sql << 'EOF'
CREATE TABLE processed_events (
    event_id       UUID        NOT NULL,
    consumer_group VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    processed_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id, consumer_group)
);
EOF

tasks.do: Wrap the consumer: dedupe check and business write in one transaction
tasks.why: One transaction is the difference between fixing the bug and relocating it.
tasks.how: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes the insert both the check and the claim: if it changed no rows, someone already processed this event and you return. Everything after it runs in the same transaction, so the mark and the work commit or roll back together.

blocks.label: notification: adapter/in/messaging/FundsHoldListener.java
notification: ProcessedEvents.java

tasks.do: Split the transaction on purpose and watch the bug come back
tasks.why: It is the only way to be sure you understand which line is doing the work.
tasks.how: Move markProcessed into its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction, then make the business write throw. The event is now marked processed but the work never happened, and the retry will skip it. Put it back afterwards, and remember the shape — it is the same bug as step 10 wearing different clothes.

blocks.label: Temporarily break it
blocks.body:
@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW)   // <- the bug
public boolean markProcessed(UUID eventId, String group) { ... }

check.run: # make the business write throw, then inspect processed_events vs sent_notifications
check.expect: A row in processed_events with no matching notification. Restore the single transaction.

tasks.do: Replay everything and verify exactly one effect each
tasks.why: This is the acceptance test for the whole step, and it is cheap to run whenever you touch a consumer.
tasks.how: Rewind the group again, let it catch up, and confirm the count has not moved. Then write the same thing as an automated test so it stays true.

blocks.label: Replay and confirm nothing moves
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-postgres psql -U ledgerflow -d notification \
  -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sent_notifications;"

kill $(lsof -ti:8082)
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk group seek notification-service --to start
./mvnw -pl services/notification-service spring-boot:run
sleep 15

docker exec -it lf-postgres psql -U ledgerflow -d notification \
  -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sent_notifications;"

check.expect: Identical. One hundred replayed events, zero extra effects.

proof.run:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda rpk group seek notification-service --to start
# wait, then count sent_notifications
proof.note: If the dedupe write and the business write are in separate transactions, you have moved the dual-write bug down a layer rather than fixed it.

doneWhen: Replaying the whole topic produces no duplicate side effects, and you have seen the bug return when you split the transaction.

lessons.title: Compound run configuration
lessons.teach: Run → Edit Configurations → + → Compound. One button starts every service you need. Stop re-launching four terminals to reproduce a duplicate.
lessons.fallbackTip: A shell script that backgrounds each service.
